key_insight: A physics-grounded welding digital twin uses fast Gaussian-process predictions to screen process settings and support simulated robotic control for future in-space metal joining.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce experimental risk by identifying promising welding conditions and control strategies before costly space-relevant testing.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates; gravity assessed separately via a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio.
Simulated six-axis UR5 welding with proportional power-setting control near an L-shaped seam corner.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; its nominal 90% intervals covered 74/80 held-out boundary-case responses, and solver re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative root-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
